title: Vireo vs llama.cpp, Mac harness
eyebrow: Vireo engine · Windows (RTX 5060 Laptop, 8 GB) · 2026-11-15 · the Mac's own harness · four small models at Q4 · build 7e00a19
headline: Vireo vs llama.cpp on a laptop GPU, with the Mac's own harness
lede: The Mac's harness of 13–14 November (bench-2026-11-13/bench.py), run unchanged on this laptop but for its paths, memory reading and contexts, on the merged build (PR #167): Gemma 4 E2B and E4B and Qwen 3.5 4B and 9B at Q4, both engines through their servers, one run each, the Mac's prompts whole except Qwen 3.5 9B's long tool log. Vireo finishes the tool task faster on all four ({tools.total}) and the skill task on three, and gets the same answers right as on the Mac. It reads every long prompt more slowly ({long.read_tps}), so its first token after one comes later and the long tool task takes longer, and it uses more of the GPU's memory. On the Mac the same harness has Vireo reading faster. The merge itself: both Qwens now finish the long tool task that failed before, and the Gemmas' tool and skill tasks are quicker.

cards.text: tool task time, Vireo vs llama.cpp: faster on all {tools.total.of} (the Mac: {mac:tools.total})
reading the ~32K prompt, Vireo vs llama.cpp: behind on all {long.read_tps.of} (the Mac: ahead, {mac:long.read_tps})

rig.label: Laptop
rig.detail: FA401GM · on mains, Turbo power plan (powercfg /getactivescheme: Turbo)

rig.label: GPU
rig.detail: 8 GB · Blackwell · driver 621.14 · at full speed: Gemma 4 E4B read medium.txt at 6,289 and 6,303 tokens/s and wrote 86.5 and 86.7 before the run

rig.label: Software
rig.detail: llama.cpp b12262 (CUDA build) · vireo-server with --context and --thinking off, as the Mac ran it

where: Agent tasks: the tool task is faster on all four ({tools.total}; Gemma 4 E4B {Gemma 4 E4B|tools.total}, where llama.cpp took {Gemma 4 E4B|llama|tools.total} s and got it wrong), the skill task on three ({skill.total}; slower on Qwen 3.5 9B, {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo|skill.total} s against {Qwen 3.5 9B|llama|skill.total} s, with 17 tool calls against 8). The long tool task is slower on all four ({longtools.total}): reading its ~56K-token log (~29K for Qwen 3.5 9B) is most of it, and Vireo reads more slowly. The Mac is ahead on all three task times ({mac:tools.total}, {mac:skill.total}, {mac:longtools.total}).

Reading: behind on every ~32K prompt, {long.read_tps}, and so on the first token after it ({long.ttft}). At ~3K tokens: level or ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|medium.read_tps}), behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|medium.read_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|medium.read_tps}). On the Mac Vireo reads the same prompts {mac:long.read_tps} faster than llama.cpp: reading long prompts is where the CUDA engine is behind.

Writing: after the ~32K prompt, ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|long.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|long.gen_tps}) and behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|long.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.gen_tps}). A short reply: ahead on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|short.gen_tps}), behind on the other three ({Gemma 4 E2B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 4B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|short.gen_tps}). Gemma 4 E2B's is one reply that took fewer of the draft model's guesses: re-checked, it wrote at 190–198 tokens/s, ahead. The Qwens have no draft model on Windows. The Mac is ahead on all four ({mac:short.gen_tps}).

Memory: Vireo uses more of the GPU on all four ({memory.gb}): {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|memory.gb} GB against {Gemma 4 E4B|llama|memory.gb} on Gemma 4 E4B, {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|memory.gb} against {Gemma 4 E2B|llama|memory.gb} on E2B. Vireo sets aside the whole context's caches when it starts (3.8 GB for Gemma 4 E4B at 65,536 tokens, by its log) and also holds the Gemmas' draft models and its skill picker; llama.cpp keeps the Gemmas' sliding-window layers short. The Mac's process peaks, 128K prompt included: {mac:memory.gb}.

Answers: Vireo {vireo_total} of 20, llama.cpp {llama_total}. Vireo's misses are exactly the Mac's, model for model: Gemma 4 E2B's tool and skill tasks, the skill task on E4B and Qwen 3.5 4B. Every model on both engines got long recall and all eight multiturn turns right, and only Qwen 3.5 9B got the skill task right (on both engines).
differs: Q4, not Q6: Google's QAT Q4_0 for the Gemmas, unsloth's Q4_K_M for the Qwens, the same GGUF files for both engines. The Mac ran Q6.

Context, 65,536 or 32,768, not 131,072: vireo-server's own choice stops at 32,768, and the Mac's ~32K prompt is 33,797 tokens on Vireo for the Gemmas and its long tool prompt ~57K. So both engines were given {Gemma 4 E2B|context} for Gemma 4 E2B, E4B and Qwen 3.5 4B, checked with Windows' GPU counters to fit without spilling into the PC's memory (context-probe.jsonl). Qwen 3.5 9B spilled at 59,392 on Vireo (its long tool prompt read at 145 tokens/s), so it ran at {Qwen 3.5 9B|context}: its ~32K prompt whole ({Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo|long.prompt} tokens), its long tool log cut to the first half (43,922 of 87,876 characters, at a line's end; inventory-sync still logs the most ERROR lines, 24 against card-reader's 13), for both engines. Every other prompt is the Mac's, whole.

No 96K or 128K rows, no mlx-vlm: an 8 GB GPU can't hold them, and mlx-vlm runs on Apple's GPUs only. So five scored tasks, not six, and llama.cpp is the only other engine. Vireo without guesses (the harness's vireo-plain) was left out: on Windows it only turns off the Gemmas' draft models and the chat's guesses, measured on their own in PR #166.
GPU memory, not the process's peak: the whole GPU's in use (nvidia-smi), read after each workload, Windows' own ~0.4 GB included; the highest is shown. The Mac's is the server process's peak.

Harness changes, Windows only: the Q4 files, llama.cpp b12262's llama-server.exe and the contexts; the folder's path written with forward slashes in the questions (a model copying C:\Users\twitc\… into a tool call can turn \t and \n into a tab and a new line: llama.cpp's skill task on Gemma 4 E4B failed five reads that way in the smoke test); Python's UTF-8 mode. The Mac runs the same file unchanged.

The Mac's columns are its run of the same harness on the same four models (results-q6-128k.jsonl, M5 Max): a different machine, quantization and context, for the direction of each difference, not its size.

panels.short: Vireo through its server, as shipped: guesses from the chat, and from Google's draft models for the Gemmas. One reply each; Gemma 4 E2B's re-checked at 190–198 tokens/s (RECHECKS.md).
panels.longwrite: The answer quotes the two hidden facts, which the chat's guesses copy.
panels.ttft: Mostly the prompt's reading. Vireo's prompt also holds its own instructions and tools (~1,300 tokens), kept from the warm-up.
panels.memory: The whole GPU, Windows' share included. Vireo's caches are set aside for the whole 65,536 (32,768 for Qwen 3.5 9B) when it starts.
panels.medium: medium.txt with a question: ~3,000 tokens read.
panels.long: long.txt whole: 32,510–33,797 tokens for the Gemmas, 29,665–31,145 for the Qwens, by each engine's count.
panels.tool: Vireo offers its own tools as well (calculate among them); llama.cpp gets the harness's five, a request per step.
panels.skill: Vireo picks the skill itself (use_skill); llama.cpp is given the skill's text in the message, as on the Mac.
panels.longtool: Vireo's Gemmas and Qwen 3.5 9B answered without a tool call, as on the Mac; llama.cpp made 1–4. Qwen 3.5 9B's log is cut to half.
panels.score: Long recall, multiturn, tool, skill, long tool, scored by the Mac's aggregate.py. The Mac had 6, with its ~96K recall.
panels.ba_tool: Faster on the Gemmas after the merge ({ba:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|tool.wall_s.change}, {ba:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|tool.wall_s.change}): tool calls written with checked guesses.
panels.ba_skill: {ba:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|skill.wall_s.change} and {ba:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|skill.wall_s.change} on the Gemmas; Gemma 4 E2B's is now right.
panels.ba_longtool: Both Qwens failed before ("A tool call ran too long"); after the merge they finish, right.
panels.ba_short: Level but for Gemma 4 E2B, one reply at 175 tokens/s (re-checked: 200).

ba_intro: Vireo only, on the rebuilt benchmark (bench_tasks.py), run twice on this laptop with identical workloads and vireo-server's own contexts (32,768; 21,504 for Qwen 3.5 9B): before the merge, this morning on 28ddaeb (bench-2026-11-15-windows-tasks); after it, on 7e00a19 (bench-2026-11-15-windows-tasks-after-merge). llama.cpp, unchanged, was run both times as a check: its task times moved {ba:llama|tool.wall_s} (tool), {ba:llama|skill.wall_s} (skill), {ba:llama|longtool.wall_s} (long tool), and it scored {ba:llama_total}.
ba_note: Before → after, one run each. Gemma 4 E2B's ~3K read ({ba:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|medium.prompt_tps}) and short reply ({ba:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|short.gen_tps}) were one-off: re-run for E2B alone, 15,773 and 200.0 again (recheck-e2b.jsonl). Gemma 4 E2B's scored tasks {ba:Gemma 4 E2B|score}: the skill task is now right; its tool and long tool tasks are still wrong.
odd: Vireo · long tool task · no tool call: on both Gemmas and Qwen 3.5 9B Vireo named inventory-sync from the log and answered without reading the README or suppliers.md, saying it had checked them (Gemma 4 E4B named suppliers that aren't in the file). The Mac's rows show the same for the same three models. The Mac's scoring checks the component's name only, so these count as right.
llama.cpp · Gemma 4 E2B · tool task: scored right by the Mac's rule (the year's total, $26,742.25, appears) but wrong: it gave every quarter $26,742.25 and the year $106,969.

Skill task: only Qwen 3.5 9B got 78 hours, on both engines. The others summed the wrong numbers (Qwen 3.5 4B on Vireo added 14 of the notes' entries to 73); llama.cpp's Gemma 4 E4B gave 84, Vireo's 97. On the Mac the same models missed it the same way.

Qwen 3.5 9B · context: at 59,392 tokens Vireo's caches spilled into the PC's memory (Windows' shared GPU memory 0.51 GB; reading 145 tokens/s), so it ran at 32,768 with its long tool log cut. llama.cpp would have held 59,392 (6.9 GB, no spill).

Gemma 4 E2B · one-off speeds: the Mac harness's short reply on Vireo (144.7 tokens/s), and the rebuilt benchmark's after-merge ~3K read (10,287) and short reply (175.0). Re-run, 190–198, 15,773 and 200.0. The rows are kept as measured; the re-checks are in RECHECKS.md.

Qwen 3.5 4B · llama.cpp · rebuilt benchmark's long tool task: still HTTP 500 after the merge (llama.cpp didn't change): its runaway calculate call cut off at 512 tokens. In the Mac harness, with its 512-token cap and a larger log, it finished.
Gemma 4 E4B · Vireo · GPU memory: 7.5 of 8 GB in use at 65,536 tokens, the most of any row; Windows' counters showed no spill.
detail_note: Context: what both engines were given. GPU memory: the whole GPU's in use (nvidia-smi), loaded and the highest after any workload. Multiturn: eight turns, each pasting a ~600-token report; first token averaged over turns 2–8.
tokens_note: Read · written · tool calls, summed over the whole task (llama.cpp's over its requests). Vireo's prompts hold its own instructions and tools; llama.cpp's holds the harness's system prompt and five tools.
method: Harness: evals/speed/bench-2026-11-13/bench.py (the Mac's, with Windows-only changes), run per model with ENGINES=vireo,llama REPS=1 and python -X utf8 -I. Results: evals/speed/bench-2026-11-15-windows-mac-harness/results.jsonl (64 rows, no errors), server logs in its bench-logs, context probe and re-checks beside it. Before and after: evals/speed/bench_tasks.py, before at 28ddaeb and after at 7e00a19. Page: evals/speed/bench_mac_harness_report.py; every number and percentage on it is worked out from those files and results-q6-128k.jsonl (the Mac's). Speeds and first-token times are the engines' own counts (vireo-server's log, llama-server's timings) and the client's clock, as on the Mac.
